transcript: Let's talk about all of the snubs and surprises from this year's Tony nominations, because, wow, were there a lot. And of course, we have to talk about Kara Young, who this year had the chance to make history as the first person to be nominated five years in a row. Having been nominated the past four years, won the past two, she was definitely a favorite to get a nom this year. And while the play that she was in, proof, was a bit divisive with critics, pretty much everyone agreed that she was the best part of it. So I was very surprised to not see her secure a nom for best Featured Actress. Proof actually was completely shut out, not nominated for a single award, which I think is criminal. Again, I know it was divisive, but I thought the acting across the board was really strong, and I said this in my video. I think ayo's performance is one of my favorite performances of the year, so it's very sad to not see her in Lead Actress of a play as well. But we did still have some history making nominations. Danny Burstein officially became the most nominated male actor, securing his ninth Tony nomination for Marjorie Prime, although he still has a ways to go if he wants to beat Audra's 11. And June Squibb made history as the oldest person ever nominated for a Tony at 96 years old for her work in Marjorie Prime! And this is actually her first Tony nomination too, which is wild. Another snub a lot of people are talking about is Lea Michele in Chess not nominated for Best Lead Actress in a musical. However, personally I think the bigger snub is not nominating Jessica Vosk in that category. But despite not getting a nomination for Lea or Best Revival of a Musical, Chess actually still did pretty well, getting a total of five nominations, including two surprise acting nominations, one for Bryce Pinkham in supporting actor and one for Hannah Cruz in supporting actress, both of which, in my opinion, very well deserved. Speaking of featured actress in a musical, I think that was the category no one correctly predicted. The biggest shock being Tempress from cats The Jellicle Ball not getting a nomination. Many people, myself included, had her as one of the locks in the category, and while yes, her role is pretty small in the show, it is such a standout moment that I was really surprised to not see it nominated. We also got a surprise down for Rachel Dratch in The Rocky Horror Show, which I am thrilled about, but I think I personally would have gone with Amber Gray instead. And then for featured Actor in a Musical, Layton Williams ended up being the actor getting in for Titanique, beating out Jim Parsons and co writer Constantine Rousoulli. It was also sad to not see Sydney James Harcourt in this category. For his performance as Rum Tum Tugger in cats the Jellicle ball. Some other surprise acting noms included Aya Cash in giant slipping into Featured Actress in a play and Brandon Dirden and Richard Thomas sneaking into Featured Actor in a play. Not to pat myself on the back, but I did predict Richard Thomas when no one else did. I may have gotten like every other nomination wrong, but I happy with that one. We also saw Sam Pinkleton stubbed from Best Director of a musical, which I think is criminal, and was also surprised to see Titanique left out of lighting design when that production was so elevated by its lighting.
classificationReason: Discussion of Tony nomination snubs and surprises across multiple shows (Proof, Marjorie Prime, etc.). No single show is the primary focus; it's a broad awards commentary spanning many productions.
